title: ReguSim: Evaluating LLM Agent Rule Grounding in Financial Compliance
abstract: arXiv:2608.19974v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: LLM agents in financial markets may cite rules yet still submit orders that violate executable constraints or misread surveillance evidence. We introduce ReguSim, a controlled financial-compliance environment, and ReguBench, a target-marked monitoring benchmark, to separate four artifacts: stated reasoning, attempted action, execution enforcement, and monitor evidence. In trader runs with DeepSeek V4 Pro and Gemini 3.5 Flash, visible rules reduce but do not eliminate rejected actions, and incentive or persona framing shifts behavior. A bridge study shows that trader rationales can mislead an independent monitor unless enforcement evidence is shown. In monitoring, simple structured baselines either match or exceed prompt-only LLMs. The results frame financial compliance evaluation as an audit of rule-grounded actions and evidence use, rather than a single compliance score.

translated_title: ReguSim：评估金融合规中LLM智能体的规则遵循能力
translated_abstract: arXiv:2608.19974v1 公告类型：新 摘要：金融市场中的LLM智能体可能会引用规则，但仍提交违反可执行约束或误读监控证据的订单。我们引入了ReguSim，一个受控的金融合规环境，以及ReguBench，一个目标标记的监控基准，以区分四个组成部分：陈述推理、尝试行动、执行强制和监控证据。在使用DeepSeek V4 Pro和Gemini 3.5 Flash的交易员运行中，可见规则减少了但并未消除被拒绝的行动，且激励或角色设定框架会改变行为。一项桥接研究表明，除非展示强制证据，否则交易员的理由可能误导独立的监控器。在监控方面，简单的结构化基线要么与仅提示的LLM持平，要么超越它们。结果将金融合规评估构建为对规则基础行动和证据使用的审计，而非单一的合规分数。
tldr: 本文提出了ReguSim和ReguBench，用于分离和审计LLM智能体在金融合规中的规则遵循、行动执行与证据使用，发现规则可见性有限且监控需依赖结构化基线。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces ReguSim and ReguBench to disentangle and audit rule grounding, action execution, and evidence use in LLM agents for financial compliance, finding that visible rules are insufficient and monitoring benefits from structured baselines.
